collection.description: An old grafter offers to make the fruit trees heavy, in return for something new to learn.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: A quiet old man named Pono comes up the path carrying a knife, a roll of bark twine and nothing else. He says he grafts fruit trees for a living, and that one afternoon's work will make the village's trees heavy with fruit. He asks only to be taught something new in return. (name1) and Pono stand under the trees, and (name1) has to decide.

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: Pono climbs like a much younger man, binding new wood to old. Before long the trees are heavy with fruit, and Pono leaves with everything (name1) could teach him.

o3.name: Outcome C
o3.text: (name1) thanks Pono and says the trees will do as they are. Pono pats the nearest trunk, as if apologizing to it, and leaves.

o2.name: Haggle, the better deal
o2.text: (name1) offers to climb the high branches so Pono need not. Pono, delighted, grafts every tree twice over, and the fruit comes in so thick the branches have to be propped up.

o2b.name: Haggle, the worse deal
o2b.text: (name1) haggles, and Pono, who hates haggling, grafts only the lowest branches before he goes home. The fruit comes, but only within easy reach.

nothing.name: Nothing to trade
nothing.text: Pono sees the trees have nowhere for new fruit to go, and leaves with a nod and nothing taken.
